title: PROSE: A Theory of Optimal Stopping with Perishable Evidence for Peer Selection in Intermittently Connected Decentralised Learning
abstract: arXiv:2609.23845v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Decentralised federated learning removes the aggregation server but makes collaboration dependent on transient peer availability. In mobile and intermittently connected systems, evaluating a promising peer consumes contact time and may cause the exchange opportunity itself to vanish, so that the evidence a learner gathers about a peer is perishable: it decays because links expire and because peer models drift while old measurements age. This paper develops a self-contained theory of optimal stopping for the resulting peer-selection problem. We formalise a receiver's within-contact decision as a finite-horizon Markov optimal-stopping problem with costly information acquisition and a future-arrival outside option, and prove that it admits an optimal policy characterised by a reservation value (Snell-envelope structure). translated_title: PROSE：间歇连接去中心化学习中基于易逝证据的对等节点选择最优停止理论
translated_abstract: 去中心化联邦学习移除了聚合服务器，但使得协作依赖于对等节点的瞬时可用性。在移动和间歇连接的系统中，评估一个有潜力的对等节点会消耗接触时间，甚至可能导致交换机会本身消失，因此学习者收集的关于对等节点的证据是易逝的：由于链路过期，以及旧测量数据老化期间对等节点模型发生漂移，证据会不断衰减。本文为由此产生的对等节点选择问题建立了一套自洽的最优停止理论。我们将接收方在接触期间的决策形式化为一个具有昂贵信息获取和未来到达外部选项的有限时域马尔可夫最优停止问题，并证明该问题存在一个由保留值（Snell包络结构）刻画的最优策略。围绕这一形式化，我们证明了：(i) 阶段一致、漂移感知的集中不等式以及一个极大极小认证规则……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文针对间歇连接去中心化学习中的对等节点选择问题，建立了考虑证据因链路过期和模型漂移而衰减的最优停止理论，证明接收方存在由保留值（Snell包络）刻画的最优停止策略，并给出漂移感知的集中不等式与极大极小认证规则。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a self-contained optimal-stopping theory for peer selection in intermittently connected decentralised learning, where evidence about peers is perishable, proving an optimal within-contact policy characterised by a reservation value (Snell envelope), along with drift-aware concentration bounds and a maximin certification rule.
